title: BackDFL: A Unified Benchmark For Backdoor Attacks and Defenses In Decentralized Federated Learning
abstract: arXiv:2608.21137v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) promises trust-free collaborative learning by replacing the centralized parameter server with peer-to-peer model exchange. However, this architectural shift fundamentally reshapes the threat landscape. Without globally coordinated aggregation, DFL becomes particularly susceptible to backdoor attacks, in which malicious participants implant persistent hidden behaviors while maintaining high clean-task performance. In this paper, we argue that the robustness of DFL has been significantly overestimated. Existing studies rely on simplified threat models, non-adaptive adversaries, fragmented evaluation protocols, inconsistent communication topologies, and ad hoc training configurations, leading to an incomplete understanding of DFL security. tldr: 本文指出去中心化联邦学习（DFL）的鲁棒性被高估，并提出了BackDFL，一个统一基准，用于在现实和适应性后门攻击下系统评估DFL的安全性。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that the robustness of Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) is overestimated and introduces BackDFL, a unified benchmark for systematically evaluating DFL security under realistic and adaptive backdoor attacks.
